Rhizopus primarily shows fluffy mold on fruit, not stem junctions. I've covered 7 classes - need one more. Let me check Bacterial Wilt.

The test image shows a tomato stem junction with prominent **grayish-white fluffy/powdery cottony growth** coating the stem, with adjacent dead/brown wilted leaves. This is the classic presentation of Botrytis cinerea (Gray Mold) infecting a stem junction.

- **Sclerotinia**: No - has black sclerotia and bleached stems
- **Southern Blight**: No - occurs at soil line with tan/brown sclerotia in white mycelium
- **Phytophthora Blight**: No - dark lesions without fluffy coating
- **Alternaria Stem Cankers**: No - dark black cankers at base
- **Late Blight**: No - dark water-soaked lesions
- **Rhizopus Soft Rots**: No - primarily affects fruit
- **Bacterial Wilt**: No - wilting without fungal growth

The grayish-white fine-grained fluffy coating at the stem junction is highly characteristic of Botrytis gray mold sporulation on tomato stems.
